elements.text:
The capnproto stuff is about optimised (de)serialisation. I am not too excited about it tbh.

However, switching from pull getblocktemplate to push is interesting.

As things stand, we wait for a blockupdate on the zmq publishing endpoint and then fetch a blocktemplate. The change to push, eliminates this round trip and bitcoind now pushes blocktemplates when certain well defined criteria are met. It is a slight optimisation, but it is in the mining loop, so could be important.

text:
`write_line(string, terminator)` also now added to the stream writers. Simplifies creation of the `http` response line, headers, and body. Also created `request` and `response` objects to encapsulate each. The `request` is passed via the notification mechanism (like p2p messages), along with the message (request body), which determines the notification type. This gives the handling protocol(s) direct access to the request while maintaining loose coupling and statelessness. The `response` object is constructed passed when a message is sent (response body).

`http` request/response only applies to `html` and `json-rpc` (Core compat) protocols, as well as the first message in a `WebSocket` upgrade. Others, including `Stratum` (vs/v2) and Electrum are just JSON over TCP - no http request/response. So those just skip the request/response serialization but are otherwise the same.

elements.text: The boost beast http request deserializer and response serializer are now integrated. There's a simple protocol class that gets attached to the channel upon connection. The channel parses the request, and dispatches the request object. The protocol subscribes to message notifications, receiving the request, and performs arbitrary processing to construct a response object, which it sends. The subscribe and send are the same as with p2p, except there is only a single message type to subscribe to and to send. For http this is sufficient, as the protocol then just handles page provisioning. It's identical to p2p processing, just sitting on top of existing structure.

elements.text: For http REST APIs (eg bitcoind JSON-RPC) we can utilize a derived channel to process the request body from json into message objects and dispatch to any number of protocols. This would make it identical at the protocols level, apart from any semantic differences, for other interfaces, such as ElectrumX and Stratum. So I think I'm going to leave this low level http processing in the network layer and implement the messages and associated protocols in node.
